slot.subtopic: Radiation pressure / momentum of EM waves
slot.brief: EM wave of given intensity falls on a perfectly absorbing (or reflecting) surface; find the radiation pressure or force on the surface.

stem: The same normally incident electromagnetic wave is fully absorbed by one surface and fully reflected by another. What are the ratios (radiation pressure on the reflecting surface / pressure on the absorbing surface; incident-wave momentum density in the two setups)?
notes: from question bank g9c80b92e8a6c (verified in job 20261127-132429-aa8a)
working:
$p_{\text{abs}}=\dfrac{I}{c},\quad p_{\text{refl}}=\dfrac{2I}{c}$
$\dfrac{p_{\text{refl}}}{p_{\text{abs}}}=2$
$u_{\text{momentum}}=\dfrac{I}{c^2}$ for the incident wave in either setup; ratio $=1$.

Independent check: For the same incident intensity I, P_abs = I/c and P_refl = 2I/c. The incident momentum density is I/c² in both setups, so the ratio is 1.
solution:
For intensity $I$, radiation pressure is $I/c$ on an absorbing surface and $2I/c$ on a reflecting surface.
$$\frac{p_{\text{refl}}}{p_{\text{abs}}}=2$$
The incident-wave momentum density is $I/c^2$ in both setups, so its ratio is $1$.
